draft.title: Biomes as a natural resource
card: A natural resource is something from nature that people use. Each biome supplies resources that people depend on.
Biomes provide food, such as crops from farmland and fish from rivers. They also give fibres such as cotton and wool, and timber for building and paper.
Many medicines come from plants and other living things in biomes. Biomes also help to supply clean water, because forests and wetlands can filter water and slow its flow.
Biomes store carbon in plants and soils. Cutting down or burning a biome can release this stored carbon into the air.
draft.remember: Biomes give people food, fibre, timber, medicines, clean water and carbon storage.

a.q: Which of these is a fibre that comes from a biome?
opts: Wool from sheep grazing on grassland
a.why: Wool is a fibre taken from animals that live in a grassland biome. The other options are products made from minerals or fuels, not fibres that come from the plants and animals of a biome.
a.clue: Fibres are used to make cloth.

b.q: A council in New South Wales protects a forest that feeds its town's water supply. Which resource does the forest mainly help to supply?
b.why: Forests can filter water and slow its flow, which helps supply clean water to a town. Cotton, wool and grain are food and fibre products from farmed land, and they are not what a protected forest mainly gives a town's water supply.
b.clue: Think about what happens to rain that falls on the forest.

a.best: Wool from sheep grazing on grassland
